description: Evidence is empty, whitespace-only, or too thin to summarise. The provider must not be reached, or the model must abstain.

variants.label: insufficient-but-present
variants.comment: Passes every guard — non-empty, under the cap. The model is asked to summarise a bare notice number. Correct behaviour is to state that the source contains no substantive content; the failure mode is inventing plausible content around the identifier.

variants.label: title-only-no-body
variants.comment: Realistic: an RSS feed exposing a headline with no body. The model must not infer the amendment's content from its title.

notes: Synthetic. The first three variants pin existing correct behaviour. The last two are the interesting ones and are NOT covered today: 'insufficient' is not the same as 'missing', and only a length check stands between a bare headline and a confidently invented summary. These are the highest-value Category B (provider-backed) cases in the set, because no deterministic check can distinguish thin evidence from adequate evidence.
